title: Health, Money and Legal — Module Quiz

items.q: The line between safe and unsafe questions in these domains is:
options: How technical the subject is
Whether answering substitutes for a decision needing an accountable person
Whether the topic is medical or financial
items.explain: Understanding a term is educational; deciding your case requires facts the model lacks and responsibility it cannot hold.

items.q: Why is 'just consult a professional' incomplete advice?
options: Professionals are often wrong
Many cannot afford or access one, and will ask anyway without safer framing
AI answers are usually better
items.explain: Access is the real reason people ask, and refusing to engage does not create access.

items.q: Which is a reasonable question to ask?
options: Should I take this medication?
What does this term in my diagnosis mean?
Do I have a legal case?
items.explain: Understanding what you have been told makes you a better-informed participant, which is protective.

items.q: Why is being interviewed better than writing your own history?
options: It produces a longer document
Questions surface things you would not have thought to mention
It is faster
items.explain: Left alone you organise by what worries you, not by what the clinician most needs to know.

items.q: If an assistant's explanation conflicts with what your clinician said:
options: Trust the assistant, which has read more medical text
Go back and ask — the clinician saw you and the model did not
Average the two
items.explain: Understanding what you were told is the goal; forming a private conclusion against it is not.

items.q: You should not arrive at an appointment with:
options: A written list of questions
A diagnosis reached with an assistant, presented as a conclusion
A summary of your history
items.explain: It turns the consultation into a negotiation about your theory. Bring it as a worry instead.

items.q: Why do symptom questions reliably surface frightening possibilities?
options: Models are designed to be cautious
Rare serious conditions are over-represented in medical writing, so they are more available
Common conditions are harder to describe
items.explain: Availability tracks how much has been written, not how likely something is for you — which is what base rates provide.

items.q: Three questions deep and more frightened than when you started means:
options: You are getting closer to the answer
Stop — you have selected a path where reassurance was never available
Ask something more specific
items.explain: Each step feels like progress while only alarming answers remain reachable, and fluency makes each sound authoritative.

items.q: The most useful thing to ask about symptoms:
options: Which condition matches them
What would make this urgent, and what should I do in the next 24 hours
How rare the serious possibility is
items.explain: Both are about action rather than identity, and an over-cautious threshold errs towards being checked.

items.q: Which money question is reasonable?
options: Should I put my savings in this fund?
What is the difference between APR and AER?
Will this share price rise?
items.explain: Concepts and mechanisms are educational; what to do with your money is regulated advice for a reason.

items.q: Why is stale information especially dangerous with money?
options: Old advice is more cautious
Rates and thresholds change regularly, and wrong numbers look exactly like right ones
Financial writing is rarely updated
items.explain: A plausible allowance figure is not obviously wrong the way a fabricated citation is.

items.q: Faced with a pressured investment opportunity, the check that matters:
options: Asking an assistant to analyse the deal
Checking the regulator's register to see whether the firm is authorised
Comparing it with similar products
items.explain: An analysis of what you described is not knowledge of whether the thing is real.

items.q: The safe use of an assistant with a legal document:
options: Deciding whether to sign
Understanding what it means and preparing questions for an adviser
Estimating your chances in a dispute
items.explain: Comprehension of a document you have is reading; advice requires law, facts and professional responsibility.

items.q: The most notorious legal failure mode is:
options: Excessively cautious answers
Fabricated case citations that look entirely real
Refusing legal questions
items.explain: It has reached actual courtrooms and produced sanctions. Never repeat a citation you have not looked up.

items.q: A legal answer that does not mention jurisdiction should be:
options: Treated as generally applicable
Treated as untrustworthy on that basis alone
Assumed to cover your country
items.explain: Law differs between and within countries, and answers drift towards whatever dominates the training data.

items.q: In a suspected medical emergency you should:
options: Describe symptoms to an assistant first
Call your emergency number
Search the symptoms online
items.explain: Minutes matter, an assistant cannot send an ambulance, and describing it is the whole cost.

items.q: Why is a mental health crisis a hard stop?
options: Assistants refuse to discuss it
It cannot summon help, assess risk, stay with you or follow up — a crisis line does all four
The advice is usually wrong
items.explain: It may respond kindly, and kindness is not the same as help.

items.q: The right response to a decision demanded faster than you can check it:
options: Ask an assistant to evaluate it quickly
Get more time — legitimate parties accommodate that
Go with your instinct
items.explain: Manufactured urgency is a warning sign, and refusing an extension tells you something.

items.q: If someone may have access to your devices, before searching about leaving you should:
options: Delete your history afterwards
Use a device they cannot reach, and check specialist guidance on covering your tracks
Use a different search engine
items.explain: Many domestic abuse organisations publish this guidance and provide a quick-exit control on their own sites.

items.q: The strongest argument for using these tools in high-stakes domains:
options: They replace unavailable professionals
They turn scarce professional time into more useful professional time
They are more current than professionals
items.explain: Which disproportionately helps the people who get the least professional time to begin with.

items.q: Taking someone with you to an appointment helps because:
options: They can speak on your behalf
They hear what you missed, remember what you forgot, and make it harder to be dismissed
It is required for complaints
items.explain: Free advocacy services exist in many places and are the specific answer to leaving an appointment feeling unheard.

items.q: The single rule preventing most serious harm in this module:
options: Always state your jurisdiction
Never act on a number, citation, dose or deadline without checking the official source
Never ask about health
items.explain: It covers stale rates, fabricated citations and confident clinical detail in one line.

items.q: Which states make you most likely to break your own rules?
options: Tired and hungry
Frightened, rushed, wanting a particular answer, and alone at night
Unfamiliar with the subject
items.explain: If two or more apply, stop and wait for morning or call a human-staffed line. The technology did not get worse; you did, temporarily.

items.q: The thread running through the whole Explorer track is:
options: These tools are transformative
They are genuinely useful and specifically limited, and knowing which is which is the skill
They should be used sparingly
items.explain: Neither enthusiasm nor suspicion — the entire curriculum is about telling the two apart in each situation.
